[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    /// Handle the keyboard navigation: WASD/arrows orbit, Q/E pan side, +/- zoom,
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    /// R reset, 1-4 view presets. Reads egui key state; writes camera goals.
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    fn handle_keys(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)        let step = 0.06_f32; // orbit radians per held frame
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        let mut any = false;
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        ui.input(|i| {
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            use egui::Key;
[475](https://docs.rs#475)            // Orbit (WASD + arrows).
[476](https://docs.rs#476)            if i.key_down(Key::A) || i.key_down(Key::ArrowLeft) {
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                self.cam.key_orbit(step, 0.0);
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                any = true;
[479](https://docs.rs#479)            }
[480](https://docs.rs#480)            if i.key_down(Key::D) || i.key_down(Key::ArrowRight) {
[481](https://docs.rs#481)                self.cam.key_orbit(-step, 0.0);
[482](https://docs.rs#482)                any = true;
[483](https://docs.rs#483)            }
[484](https://docs.rs#484)            if i.key_down(Key::W) || i.key_down(Key::ArrowUp) {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                self.cam.key_orbit(0.0, step);
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                any = true;
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            }
[488](https://docs.rs#488)            if i.key_down(Key::S) || i.key_down(Key::ArrowDown) {
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                self.cam.key_orbit(0.0, -step);
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                any = true;
[491](https://docs.rs#491)            }
[492](https://docs.rs#492)            // Zoom.
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            if i.key_down(Key::Plus) || i.key_down(Key::Equals) {
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                self.cam.dolly(40.0, None);
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                any = true;
[496](https://docs.rs#496)            }
[497](https://docs.rs#497)            if i.key_down(Key::Minus) {
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                self.cam.dolly(-40.0, None);
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                any = true;
[500](https://docs.rs#500)            }
[501](https://docs.rs#501)            // Reset + presets (edge-triggered).
[502](https://docs.rs#502)            if i.key_pressed(Key::R) {
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                self.cam.reset();
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                any = true;
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            }
[506](https://docs.rs#506)            if i.key_pressed(Key::Num1) {
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                self.cam.apply_preset(ViewPreset::Top);
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                any = true;
[509](https://docs.rs#509)            }
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            if i.key_pressed(Key::Num2) {
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                self.cam.apply_preset(ViewPreset::Isometric);
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                any = true;
[513](https://docs.rs#513)            }
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            if i.key_pressed(Key::Num3) {
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                self.cam.apply_preset(ViewPreset::Oblique);
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                any = true;
[517](https://docs.rs#517)            }
[518](https://docs.rs#518)            if i.key_pressed(Key::Num4) {
[519](https://docs.rs#519)                self.cam.apply_preset(ViewPreset::Front);
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                any = true;
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            }
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        });
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        if any {
[524](https://docs.rs#524)            self.spin = false;
[525](https://docs.rs#525)        }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    }
[527](https://docs.rs#527)

[553](https://docs.rs#553)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    /// Rotate a point by yaw (Y) then tilt (X). Returns `(x, y, z)` view-space.
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    /// **Legacy** helper kept for callers that did fixed-orbit projection before
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    /// the [`OrbitCamera`]; the live render path now uses the camera. Identical
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// convention to [`RabbitLogo3D`] so the logo + map agree.
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    pub fn rotate(p: [f32; 3], yaw: f32, tilt: f32) -> [f32; 3] {
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        let x1 = p[0] * cy + p[2] * sy;
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        let z1 = -p[0] * sy + p[2] * cy;
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        let (st, ct) = tilt.sin_cos();
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        let y2 = p[1] * ct - z1 * st;
[564](https://docs.rs#564)        let z2 = p[1] * st + z1 * ct;
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        [x1, y2, z2]
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    }
[567](https://docs.rs#567)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// The camera actually projected this frame: the live [`Self::cam`], but with
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// the auto-spin (and any injected clock) folded into its azimuth so a fixed
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    /// clock yields a pure, reproducible orbit. Pan/zoom/preset state is preserved.
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    pub fn render_camera(&self) -> OrbitCamera {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let mut c = self.cam.clone();
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        if self.spin {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            let spin = self.clock_s.map(|t| t as f32 * self.spin_rate).unwrap_or(0.0);
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            c.azimuth += spin;
[576](https://docs.rs#576)            c.goal_azimuth = c.azimuth;
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        }
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        c
[579](https://docs.rs#579)    }
[580](https://docs.rs#580)
[581](https://docs.rs#581)    /// Project + frustum/back-face cull + depth-sort + light the extruded mesh
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    /// into screen-space shaded faces via the **perspective orbit camera**. Pure
[583](https://docs.rs#583)    /// (no egui) so the self-test can count *visible lit triangles* without a UI.
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Returns `(camera_depth, [3 px], shaded_color)` per visible tri, far→near.
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    ///
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// `center` is the viewport centre in pixels; `scale` is the projection
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// half-height in pixels (≈ half the viewport height) — the perspective focal
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// scale. `base` is the **atmospheric fog colour** (the background): distant
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// faces are blended toward it so the city recedes into haze — the subtle depth
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// cue that, with the directional light, makes the model read as a 3D city
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    /// rather than a flat field of prisms. The per-triangle source colour drives the
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// lit tint; fog only desaturates it with distance.
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    pub fn shade_faces(&self, center: Pos2, scale: f32, base: Color32) -> Vec<(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)> {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        self.shade_faces_clip(center, scale, base, true)
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    /// **Diagnostic / regression variant** of [`Self::shade_faces`] with the step-1
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    /// view-space near clip togglable. `near_clip = true` is the production path
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    /// (the FIX); `near_clip = false` reproduces the *pre-fix* pipeline — the
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    /// brittle "drop the whole triangle if any vertex is behind the eye" +
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    /// "screen-extent guard" heuristics — so a fail-on-bug / pass-on-fix test can
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    /// inject the same camera pose into both and compare the escaping geometry the
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// rect-scissor is then handed. Not for production callers; the bug oracle test
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    /// uses it to prove the fix changes the geometry that reaches the rasterizer.
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    pub fn shade_faces_clip(
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        &self,
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        center: Pos2,
[608](https://docs.rs#608)        scale: f32,
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        base: Color32,
[610](https://docs.rs#610)        near_clip: bool,
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ) -> Vec<(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)> {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)        if !near_clip {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)            return self.shade_faces_legacy(center, scale, base);
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        let cam = self.render_camera();
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        let half_h = scale.max(1.0);
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        let centre = (center.x, center.y);
[618](https://docs.rs#618)        let near = OrbitCamera::NEAR_PLANE;
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        // Frustum side-plane slope = tan(fov_y/2): `project_view` uses
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        // `focal = half_h / tan(fov_y/2)`, so a vertex with `|cx/cz| <= tan(fov_y/2)`
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        // projects to EXACTLY `center ± half_h` (the viewport edge) — the tight bound.
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        // (sx == sy here = the square viewport at half_h; the rect-scissor trims any
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        // non-square remainder.)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        let fslope = (cam.fov_y * 0.5).tan().max(1e-4);
[625](https://docs.rs#625)
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        // ── STEP 1: view-space transform (once; reused index buffer) ────────────
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        // Transform every vertex into VIEW space (x=right, y=up, z=forward). The
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        // near-plane clip (step 1) operates here, BEFORE the perspective divide, so
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        // a triangle straddling the eye is split — its in-front part kept, its
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        // behind-the-eye part dropped — instead of either projecting to a wild
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        // off-screen smear or being dropped whole (the bug). Projection (step 2)
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        // then divides only safe `cz > near` depths.
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        let view: Vec<V3> =
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            self.mesh.positions.iter().map(|&p| cam.view_space(V3::new(p[0], p[1], p[2]))).collect();
[635](https://docs.rs#635)
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        // Light from the upper-front-left, in WORLD space (camera-independent so
[637](https://docs.rs#637)        // the model's faces keep their identity as the camera orbits).
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        let light = {
[639](https://docs.rs#639)            let l = [-0.4f32, 0.7, 0.6];
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            let n = (l[0] * l[0] + l[1] * l[1] + l[2] * l[2]).sqrt();
[641](https://docs.rs#641)            [l[0] / n, l[1] / n, l[2] / n]
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        };
[643](https://docs.rs#643)
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        // ── atmospheric depth fog ──────────────────────────────────────────────
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        // Faces far from the eye fade toward the background colour so the city
[646](https://docs.rs#646)        // recedes into haze (a classic depth cue). The fog ramps across a band
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        // centred on the camera distance: `fog_near` ≈ the foreground (no haze),
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        // `fog_far` ≈ well behind the target (max haze). Tuned shallow so the
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        // foreground stays crisp and only the far skyline softens.
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        let fog = [base.r() as f32, base.g() as f32, base.b() as f32];
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        let fog_near = (cam.distance * 0.6).max(0.1);
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        let fog_far = cam.distance * 2.2 + 0.5;
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        let fog_span = (fog_far - fog_near).max(1e-3);
[654](https://docs.rs#654)        // Cap the maximum haze so distant buildings never vanish entirely.
[655](https://docs.rs#655)        const FOG_MAX: f32 = 0.55;
[656](https://docs.rs#656)
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        let n_tris = self.mesh.indices.len() / 3;
[658](https://docs.rs#658)        let mut faces: Vec<(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)> = Vec::with_capacity(n_tris);
[659](https://docs.rs#659)
[660](https://docs.rs#660)        // ── STEP 2b: the **screen-extent frustum bound** (the SECOND half of the
[661](https://docs.rs#661)        // fix). The view-space near clip (step 1) guarantees every surviving vertex
[662](https://docs.rs#662)        // has `cz > near`, so projection is finite — but with a tiny near plane a
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        // face grazing the near plane far off-axis still projects to a coordinate a
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        // huge multiple of the viewport (cz≈near, cx large ⇒ cx/cz·focal ≈ tens of
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        // thousands of px). The widget rect scissor confines that to the rect, but a
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        // single 20 000-px terrain triangle clipped to the rect becomes a giant
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        // wedge that FILLS the component — the green smear in the screenshot
[668](https://docs.rs#668)        // (geometrically "inside the rect", visually the bug). Clip every projected
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        // face to a generous screen box (the viewport expanded by `SCREEN_BOUND_K`)
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        // BEFORE depth-sort so `max_projected_extent ≤ viewport · 2·K` holds by
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        // construction: the off-screen excess that would smear is removed, while any
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        // genuinely on-screen face is untouched. Same ceiling the `no_spokes` fence
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        // asserts (half_h·8). Left/right use the full width (≈2·half_h ⇒ a square-ish
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        // viewport); the bound is intentionally loose so it never clips real geometry.
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        const SCREEN_BOUND_K: f32 = 1.0;
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        let screen_bound = egui::Rect::from_min_max(
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            Pos2::new(centre.0 - SCREEN_BOUND_K * half_h, centre.1 - SCREEN_BOUND_K * half_h),
[678](https://docs.rs#678)            Pos2::new(centre.0 + SCREEN_BOUND_K * half_h, centre.1 + SCREEN_BOUND_K * half_h),
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        );
[680](https://docs.rs#680)
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        // Emit counters (cheap; stripped in release) for the part-step oracles.
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        let mut em = ShadeEmit::default();
[684](https://docs.rs#684)
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        for t in 0..n_tris {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            let i0 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3] as usize;
[687](https://docs.rs#687)            let i1 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3 + 1] as usize;
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            let i2 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3 + 2] as usize;
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            let vtri = [view[i0], view[i1], view[i2]];
[690](https://docs.rs#690)
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            // ── STEP 1: view-space near-plane clip (the FIX) ────────────────────
[692](https://docs.rs#692)            // Split the triangle against z = near in VIEW space. A triangle wholly
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            // behind the eye clips to empty (dropped); one straddling the plane is
[694](https://docs.rs#694)            // cut to a 3..4-gon whose every vertex is in front — so projection can
[695](https://docs.rs#695)            // never divide by a near-zero depth and smear off the rect.
[696](https://docs.rs#696)            // FULL frustum clip (near + 4 sides) — bounds lateral projection to the
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            // viewport by construction, killing the off-axis-near spoke smear that a
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            // near-only clip leaves (measured up to 84 000px before this). sx=sy=1.0 =
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            // the square frustum at focal half_h (project_view's focal); the final
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            // rect-scissor handles any non-square remainder.
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            let (poly, crossed) = clip_tri_frustum(&vtri, near, fslope, fslope);
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[703](https://docs.rs#703)            {
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                em.near_in += 1;
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                if poly.len() < 3 {
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                    em.near_dropped += 1;
[707](https://docs.rs#707)                }
[708](https://docs.rs#708)                if crossed {
[709](https://docs.rs#709)                    em.near_crossing_split += 1;
[710](https://docs.rs#710)                }
[711](https://docs.rs#711)                // Oracle: NO surviving clipped vertex sits on/behind the eye.
[712](https://docs.rs#712)                if poly.iter().any(|p| p.z < near - 1e-4) {
[713](https://docs.rs#713)                    em.near_behind_survived += 1;
[714](https://docs.rs#714)                }
[715](https://docs.rs#715)            }
[716](https://docs.rs#716)            #[cfg(not(feature = "testmatrix"))]
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            let _ = crossed;
[718](https://docs.rs#718)            if poly.len() < 3 {
[719](https://docs.rs#719)                continue;
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            }
[721](https://docs.rs#721)
[722](https://docs.rs#722)            // ── STEP 2: project the clipped view-space polygon to screen px ──────
[723](https://docs.rs#723)            // Every point has z > near (step 1 guaranteed it), so the divide is
[724](https://docs.rs#724)            // safe and bounded.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)            let mut sp: Vec<Projected> = Vec::with_capacity(poly.len());
[726](https://docs.rs#726)            for v in &poly {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)                sp.push(cam.project_view(*v, centre, half_h));
[728](https://docs.rs#728)            }
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[730](https://docs.rs#730)            {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)                em.project_in += poly.len();
[732](https://docs.rs#732)                em.project_out += sp.len();
[733](https://docs.rs#733)                if sp.iter().any(|p| p.x.is_nan() || p.y.is_nan()) {
[734](https://docs.rs#734)                    em.project_nan += 1;
[735](https://docs.rs#735)                }
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            }
[737](https://docs.rs#737)
[738](https://docs.rs#738)            // Per-face flat normal (averaged vertex normals) + source colour — the
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            // same shading the unclipped face had; all sub-triangles share it.
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            let nv = {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)                let n0 = self.mesh.normals[i0];
[742](https://docs.rs#742)                let n1 = self.mesh.normals[i1];
[743](https://docs.rs#743)                let n2 = self.mesh.normals[i2];
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                let mut nx = n0[0] + n1[0] + n2[0];
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                let mut ny = n0[1] + n1[1] + n2[1];
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                let mut nz = n0[2] + n1[2] + n2[2];
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                let len = (nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz).sqrt().max(1e-6);
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                nx /= len;
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                ny /= len;
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                nz /= len;
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                [nx, ny, nz]
[752](https://docs.rs#752)            };
[753](https://docs.rs#753)            let diff = (nv[0] * light[0] + nv[1] * light[1] + nv[2] * light[2]).abs();
[754](https://docs.rs#754)            let shade = (0.30 + 0.70 * diff).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
[755](https://docs.rs#755)            let src = self.mesh.colors[t];
[756](https://docs.rs#756)
[757](https://docs.rs#757)            // Fan-triangulate the clipped polygon (0→i→i+1) into sub-triangles.
[758](https://docs.rs#758)            for k in 1..poly.len() - 1 {
[759](https://docs.rs#759)                let (pa, pb, pc) = (sp[0], sp[k], sp[k + 1]);
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                // ── STEP 3: far-plane frustum cull (near is the clip's job now) ──
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                {
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                    em.cull_in += 1;
[764](https://docs.rs#764)                }
[765](https://docs.rs#765)                if !pa.visible || !pb.visible || !pc.visible {
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                    #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                    {
[768](https://docs.rs#768)                        em.cull_far_dropped += 1;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)                    }
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                    continue;
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                }
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                // ── STEP 4: screen-space back-face cull (CCW-front) ─────────────
[773](https://docs.rs#773)                let cross_z = (pb.x - pa.x) * (pc.y - pa.y) - (pb.y - pa.y) * (pc.x - pa.x);
[774](https://docs.rs#774)                if cross_z <= 0.0 {
[775](https://docs.rs#775)                    #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[776](https://docs.rs#776)                    {
[777](https://docs.rs#777)                        em.cull_backface_dropped += 1;
[778](https://docs.rs#778)                    }
[779](https://docs.rs#779)                    continue;
[780](https://docs.rs#780)                }
[781](https://docs.rs#781)                #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[782](https://docs.rs#782)                {
[783](https://docs.rs#783)                    em.cull_out += 1;
[784](https://docs.rs#784)                }
[785](https://docs.rs#785)
[786](https://docs.rs#786)                // ── STEP 5: shade (fog + directional light) ─────────────────────
[787](https://docs.rs#787)                let depth = (pa.depth + pb.depth + pc.depth) / 3.0;
[788](https://docs.rs#788)                let (lr, lg, lb) = (src.r() as f32 * shade, src.g() as f32 * shade, src.b() as f32 * shade);
[789](https://docs.rs#789)                let fog_t = (((depth - fog_near) / fog_span).clamp(0.0, 1.0)) * FOG_MAX;
[790](https://docs.rs#790)                let col = Color32::from_rgb(
[791](https://docs.rs#791)                    (lr + (fog[0] - lr) * fog_t) as u8,
[792](https://docs.rs#792)                    (lg + (fog[1] - lg) * fog_t) as u8,
[793](https://docs.rs#793)                    (lb + (fog[2] - lb) * fog_t) as u8,
[794](https://docs.rs#794)                );
[795](https://docs.rs#795)                #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[796](https://docs.rs#796)                {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)                    em.shade_out += 1;
[798](https://docs.rs#798)                    if shade > 0.31 {
[799](https://docs.rs#799)                        em.shade_lit += 1;
[800](https://docs.rs#800)                    }
[801](https://docs.rs#801)                }
[802](https://docs.rs#802)                // ── STEP 2b applied: clip the projected face to the screen bound so
[803](https://docs.rs#803)                // no emitted triangle can exceed the viewport·K extent (kills the
[804](https://docs.rs#804)                // grazing-near-plane smear wedge). A face fully inside is returned
[805](https://docs.rs#805)                // unchanged (3 verts); one poking past the bound is trimmed to a
[806](https://docs.rs#806)                // convex polygon we fan back into triangles; one fully outside is
[807](https://docs.rs#807)                // dropped. The widget rect scissor (step 7) confines further at paint.
[808](https://docs.rs#808)                let tri = [Pos2::new(pa.x, pa.y), Pos2::new(pb.x, pb.y), Pos2::new(pc.x, pc.y)];
[809](https://docs.rs#809)                let bounded = clip_poly_to_rect(&tri, screen_bound);
[810](https://docs.rs#810)                if bounded.len() < 3 {
[811](https://docs.rs#811)                    #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[812](https://docs.rs#812)                    {
[813](https://docs.rs#813)                        em.bound_dropped += 1;
[814](https://docs.rs#814)                    }
[815](https://docs.rs#815)                    continue;
[816](https://docs.rs#816)                }
[817](https://docs.rs#817)                #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[818](https://docs.rs#818)                if bounded.len() != 3 || bounded != tri.to_vec() {
[819](https://docs.rs#819)                    em.bound_trimmed += 1;
[820](https://docs.rs#820)                }
[821](https://docs.rs#821)                for j in 1..bounded.len() - 1 {
[822](https://docs.rs#822)                    let f = [bounded[0], bounded[j], bounded[j + 1]];
[823](https://docs.rs#823)                    #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[824](https://docs.rs#824)                    {
[825](https://docs.rs#825)                        let ex = f[0].x.max(f[1].x).max(f[2].x) - f[0].x.min(f[1].x).min(f[2].x);
[826](https://docs.rs#826)                        let ey = f[0].y.max(f[1].y).max(f[2].y) - f[0].y.min(f[1].y).min(f[2].y);
[827](https://docs.rs#827)                        em.max_extent_px = em.max_extent_px.max(ex.max(ey));
[828](https://docs.rs#828)                    }
[829](https://docs.rs#829)                    faces.push((depth, f, col));
[830](https://docs.rs#830)                }
[831](https://docs.rs#831)            }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        }
[833](https://docs.rs#833)        // ── STEP 6: depth-sort (painter's algorithm: far first, near last) ──────
[834](https://docs.rs#834)        faces.sort_by(|l, r| r.0.partial_cmp(&l.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
[835](https://docs.rs#835)
[836](https://docs.rs#836)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[837](https://docs.rs#837)        {
[838](https://docs.rs#838)            // is_monotone: the sorted depths are non-increasing (far→near).
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            let mut monotone = true;
[840](https://docs.rs#840)            for w in faces.windows(2) {
[841](https://docs.rs#841)                if w[0].0 < w[1].0 - 1e-3 {
[842](https://docs.rs#842)                    monotone = false;
[843](https://docs.rs#843)                    break;
[844](https://docs.rs#844)                }
[845](https://docs.rs#845)            }
[846](https://docs.rs#846)            em.depth_monotone = monotone;
[847](https://docs.rs#847)            em.emit_steps("facett-map3d", half_h);
[848](https://docs.rs#848)        }
[849](https://docs.rs#849)        faces
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    }
[851](https://docs.rs#851)
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// The **pre-fix** projection pipeline (diagnostic only) — kept so the bug
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// oracle test can reproduce the geometry the brittle heuristics produced. It
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    /// projects all three raw vertices, drops the triangle whole if any vertex is
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    /// behind the eye, and applies the old "screen-extent guard" (reject a face
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    /// whose projected extent dwarfs the viewport). A face *straddling* the near
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    /// plane that survives the guard still smears far off the rect — exactly the
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    /// escaping geometry the step-1 near clip eliminates.
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    fn shade_faces_legacy(&self, center: Pos2, scale: f32, base: Color32) -> Vec<(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)> {
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        let cam = self.render_camera();
[861](https://docs.rs#861)        let half_h = scale.max(1.0);
[862](https://docs.rs#862)        let centre = (center.x, center.y);
[863](https://docs.rs#863)        let proj: Vec<Projected> = self
[864](https://docs.rs#864)            .mesh
[865](https://docs.rs#865)            .positions
[866](https://docs.rs#866)            .iter()
[867](https://docs.rs#867)            .map(|&p| cam.project(V3::new(p[0], p[1], p[2]), centre, half_h))
[868](https://docs.rs#868)            .collect();
[869](https://docs.rs#869)        let light = {
[870](https://docs.rs#870)            let l = [-0.4f32, 0.7, 0.6];
[871](https://docs.rs#871)            let n = (l[0] * l[0] + l[1] * l[1] + l[2] * l[2]).sqrt();
[872](https://docs.rs#872)            [l[0] / n, l[1] / n, l[2] / n]
[873](https://docs.rs#873)        };
[874](https://docs.rs#874)        let fog = [base.r() as f32, base.g() as f32, base.b() as f32];
[875](https://docs.rs#875)        let fog_near = (cam.distance * 0.6).max(0.1);
[876](https://docs.rs#876)        let fog_far = cam.distance * 2.2 + 0.5;
[877](https://docs.rs#877)        let fog_span = (fog_far - fog_near).max(1e-3);
[878](https://docs.rs#878)        const FOG_MAX: f32 = 0.55;
[879](https://docs.rs#879)        let n_tris = self.mesh.indices.len() / 3;
[880](https://docs.rs#880)        let mut faces: Vec<(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)> = Vec::with_capacity(n_tris);
[881](https://docs.rs#881)        for t in 0..n_tris {
[882](https://docs.rs#882)            let i0 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3] as usize;
[883](https://docs.rs#883)            let i1 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3 + 1] as usize;
[884](https://docs.rs#884)            let i2 = self.mesh.indices[t * 3 + 2] as usize;
[885](https://docs.rs#885)            let (pa, pb, pc) = (proj[i0], proj[i1], proj[i2]);
[886](https://docs.rs#886)            if !pa.visible || !pb.visible || !pc.visible {
[887](https://docs.rs#887)                continue;
[888](https://docs.rs#888)            }
[889](https://docs.rs#889)            // Old screen-extent guard (the heuristic the fix replaces).
[890](https://docs.rs#890)            let ext_x = pa.x.max(pb.x).max(pc.x) - pa.x.min(pb.x).min(pc.x);
[891](https://docs.rs#891)            let ext_y = pa.y.max(pb.y).max(pc.y) - pa.y.min(pb.y).min(pc.y);
[892](https://docs.rs#892)            if ext_x > half_h * 6.0 || ext_y > half_h * 6.0 {
[893](https://docs.rs#893)                continue;
[894](https://docs.rs#894)            }
[895](https://docs.rs#895)            let cross_z = (pb.x - pa.x) * (pc.y - pa.y) - (pb.y - pa.y) * (pc.x - pa.x);
[896](https://docs.rs#896)            if cross_z <= 0.0 {
[897](https://docs.rs#897)                continue;
[898](https://docs.rs#898)            }
[899](https://docs.rs#899)            let nv = {
[900](https://docs.rs#900)                let n0 = self.mesh.normals[i0];
[901](https://docs.rs#901)                let n1 = self.mesh.normals[i1];
[902](https://docs.rs#902)                let n2 = self.mesh.normals[i2];
[903](https://docs.rs#903)                let mut nx = n0[0] + n1[0] + n2[0];
[904](https://docs.rs#904)                let mut ny = n0[1] + n1[1] + n2[1];
[905](https://docs.rs#905)                let mut nz = n0[2] + n1[2] + n2[2];
[906](https://docs.rs#906)                let len = (nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz).sqrt().max(1e-6);
[907](https://docs.rs#907)                nx /= len;
[908](https://docs.rs#908)                ny /= len;
[909](https://docs.rs#909)                nz /= len;
[910](https://docs.rs#910)                [nx, ny, nz]
[911](https://docs.rs#911)            };
[912](https://docs.rs#912)            let diff = (nv[0] * light[0] + nv[1] * light[1] + nv[2] * light[2]).abs();
[913](https://docs.rs#913)            let shade = (0.30 + 0.70 * diff).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
[914](https://docs.rs#914)            let src = self.mesh.colors[t];
[915](https://docs.rs#915)            let depth = (pa.depth + pb.depth + pc.depth) / 3.0;
[916](https://docs.rs#916)            let (lr, lg, lb) = (src.r() as f32 * shade, src.g() as f32 * shade, src.b() as f32 * shade);
[917](https://docs.rs#917)            let fog_t = (((depth - fog_near) / fog_span).clamp(0.0, 1.0)) * FOG_MAX;
[918](https://docs.rs#918)            let col = Color32::from_rgb(
[919](https://docs.rs#919)                (lr + (fog[0] - lr) * fog_t) as u8,
[920](https://docs.rs#920)                (lg + (fog[1] - lg) * fog_t) as u8,
[921](https://docs.rs#921)                (lb + (fog[2] - lb) * fog_t) as u8,
[922](https://docs.rs#922)            );
[923](https://docs.rs#923)            faces.push((depth, [Pos2::new(pa.x, pa.y), Pos2::new(pb.x, pb.y), Pos2::new(pc.x, pc.y)], col));
[924](https://docs.rs#924)        }
[925](https://docs.rs#925)        faces.sort_by(|l, r| r.0.partial_cmp(&l.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
[926](https://docs.rs#926)        faces
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    }
[928](https://docs.rs#928)}
[929](https://docs.rs#929)
[930](https://docs.rs#930)#[cfg(feature = "wgpu")]
[931](https://docs.rs#931)impl Map3D {
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// GPU **depth-tested** render path: add the egui_wgpu paint callback that
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    /// renders the extruded mesh into an offscreen colour + depth32 target with a
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    /// real Z-buffer (`CompareFunction::Less`), then blits it into egui's pass.
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// Returns `true` if the callback was added (host opted in + a renderer is
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    /// installed), `false` to fall back to the CPU painter.
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    fn draw_map_gpu(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, rect: egui::Rect, bg: egui::Color32) -> bool {
[938](https://docs.rs#938)        if !self.use_gpu || self.mesh.indices.is_empty() {
[939](https://docs.rs#939)            return false;
[940](https://docs.rs#940)        }
[941](https://docs.rs#941)        let cam = self.render_camera();
[942](https://docs.rs#942)        let aspect = (rect.width() / rect.height().max(1e-3)).max(1e-3);
[943](https://docs.rs#943)        let view_proj = cam.view_proj(aspect);
[944](https://docs.rs#944)        // Inverse view-projection for the skybox pass (NDC → world view ray). A
[945](https://docs.rs#945)        // degenerate camera matrix (never expected) falls back to identity → the sky
[946](https://docs.rs#946)        // pass still runs but reconstructs no parallax; the mesh draws over it.
[947](https://docs.rs#947)        let inv_view_proj = sky::invert(&view_proj).unwrap_or({
[948](https://docs.rs#948)            let mut id = [0.0f32; 16];
[949](https://docs.rs#949)            id[0] = 1.0;
[950](https://docs.rs#950)            id[5] = 1.0;
[951](https://docs.rs#951)            id[10] = 1.0;
[952](https://docs.rs#952)            id[15] = 1.0;
[953](https://docs.rs#953)            id
[954](https://docs.rs#954)        });
[955](https://docs.rs#955)
[956](https://docs.rs#956)        // World-space sun + sky (Phase 1 PBR): the single lighting model the GPU
[957](https://docs.rs#957)        // shader + CPU painter share. `light` = sun dir + ambient.
[958](https://docs.rs#958)        let light = self.sun.light_uniform();
[959](https://docs.rs#959)        let sun_color = self.sun.sun_uniform();
[960](https://docs.rs#960)        let sky_color = self.sun.sky_uniform();
[961](https://docs.rs#961)        let eye = { let e = cam.eye(); [e.x, e.y, e.z, 0.0] };
[962](https://docs.rs#962)        // PBR: matte building/ground roughness, dielectric (non-metal); time drives
[963](https://docs.rs#963)        // the (Phase 2) water waves — injected clock keeps blobs deterministic.
[964](https://docs.rs#964)        let time = self.clock_s.unwrap_or(0.0) as f32;
[965](https://docs.rs#965)        // Height-fog density k rides in pbr.w (the shader reads fog_range.z from it).
[966](https://docs.rs#966)        let pbr = [0.62f32, 0.0, time, 1.4];
[967](https://docs.rs#967)        // ── Cascaded shadow maps (T3.3) ──
[968](https://docs.rs#968)        // The box is `[-1,1]³`; fit THREE concentric orthographic cascades around the
[969](https://docs.rs#969)        // scene centre — tight (high-res, crisp near contacts) → wide (coarse, softer
[970](https://docs.rs#970)        // far) — and select per-fragment by camera depth. `shadow_strength` gates how
[971](https://docs.rs#971)        // dark casts get; `soft_shadows` switches PCSS on (vs a hard PCF control).
[972](https://docs.rs#972)        let centre = [0.0, 0.4, 0.0];
[973](https://docs.rs#973)        let light_vp = [
[974](https://docs.rs#974)            self.sun.light_view_proj(centre, 0.75),
[975](https://docs.rs#975)            self.sun.light_view_proj(centre, 1.35),
[976](https://docs.rs#976)            self.sun.light_view_proj(centre, 2.40),
[977](https://docs.rs#977)        ];
[978](https://docs.rs#978)        // Camera-depth split distances (cascade0→1, cascade1→2), scaled to the dolly.
[979](https://docs.rs#979)        let cascade_splits = [cam.distance * 0.85, cam.distance * 1.6];
[980](https://docs.rs#980)        // PCSS softness scale (cascade.z): how fast the penumbra grows with the
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        // occluder→receiver gap. Generous so the contact-hardening penumbra is a real,
[982](https://docs.rs#982)        // visible soft band (sharp at contact, wide at the shadow tip). The blocker
[983](https://docs.rs#983)        // SEARCH radius is a separate small fixed value in the shader (so flat lit
[984](https://docs.rs#984)        // ground never self-shadows), this only scales the final filter width.
[985](https://docs.rs#985)        let light_size = 0.45_f32;
[986](https://docs.rs#986)        let shadow_strength = self.shadow_strength;
[987](https://docs.rs#987)        let soft_shadows = self.soft_shadows;
[988](https://docs.rs#988)        // ── SSAO (T3.1) ── radius in design units (small, design-box scene) + strength.
[989](https://docs.rs#989)        let ssao_on = self.ssao;
[990](https://docs.rs#990)        let ssao_radius = 0.16_f32;
[991](https://docs.rs#991)        let ssao_intensity = 2.4_f32;
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        // ── Reflective water (Phase 2): the altitude LOD trigger ──
[993](https://docs.rs#993)        // water_on when there is water geometry AND the tier is Ground (alt < 300 m)
[994](https://docs.rs#994)        // — the headline. reflect_on adds the planar reflection pass (native; the
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        // wasm path keeps water_on but reflect_on=false → sky-gradient reflection).
[996](https://docs.rs#996)        let water_on = self.water_active();
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        let reflect_on = water_on && self.planar_reflection; // wasm: sky-fallback.
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        let refl_vp = cam.view_proj_mirrored(aspect, extrude::WATER_HEIGHT);
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        // Water tints + wave/foam params. shallow→deep, amplitude, steepness; foam,
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)        // max-depth (NDC), base wavelength. Amplitude is tiny (design-unit scene).
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)        let water_shallow = [0.18f32, 0.42, 0.52, 0.0020]; // teal shallows + small amp
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)        let water_deep = [0.02f32, 0.10, 0.20, 0.28]; // deep navy + gentle steepness
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        let water_params = [0.45f32, 0.004, 0.14, 0.0]; // foam, max-depth-NDC, wavelength
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)        let clear = {
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)            let [r, g, b, a] = bg.to_array();
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)            [f32::from(r) / 255.0, f32::from(g) / 255.0, f32::from(b) / 255.0, f32::from(a) / 255.0]
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)        };
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)        // Camera-relative fog ramp (matches the CPU painter): no haze in the
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)        // foreground, easing in only well behind the framed target so the far
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)        // skyline softens. Keyed to the dolly distance so it scales with the view.
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        let fog = [cam.distance * 0.6, cam.distance * 2.2 + 0.5, 0.55, 0.0];
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)        let ppp = ui.ctx().pixels_per_point();
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        let px_w = (rect.width() * ppp).round().max(1.0) as u32;
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)        let px_h = (rect.height() * ppp).round().max(1.0) as u32;
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)        // Build + cache the GPU payload once; re-send it for the first few frames
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)        // so it reaches the device even though kittest only `prepare`s the last
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)        // frame's callbacks. The renderer ignores re-uploads once it has a vbuf.
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)        if self.gpu_geom.is_none() {
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)            self.gpu_geom =
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)                Some(std::rc::Rc::new(gpu::build_gpu_geometry_with_water(&self.mesh, &self.water)));
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)        }
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)        // Always carry the payload. The renderer's `upload` is idempotent (it keeps
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)        // the first vbuf), so this is a cheap Rc clone of a pre-built buffer — and
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        // it guarantees the geometry reaches the device regardless of which frame
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)        // the host's wgpu backend actually `prepare`s (kittest preps only the last).
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        let geometry = self.gpu_geom.as_ref().map(|g| Box::new((**g).clone()));
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        // Add the callback through the **rect-clipped** painter so the callback's
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)        // `clip_rect` is the widget rect (matching the CPU painter's `painter_at`),
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)        // not the panel-wide painter clip. The GPU pass then scissors to the
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)        // viewport ∩ clip_rect (see `Map3dPaintCallback::paint` / `gpu_scissor_px`),
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)        // confining every painted pixel to this component — FIX (a).
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)        ui.painter_at(rect).add(egui_wgpu::Callback::new_paint_callback(
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)            rect,
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)            gpu::Map3dPaintCallback {
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)                geometry, view_proj, inv_view_proj, sky_on: self.sky,
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)                light, clear, fog, sun_color, sky_color, eye, pbr,
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)                light_vp, cascade_splits, light_size, soft_shadows, shadow_strength,
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                ssao_on, ssao_radius, ssao_intensity,
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                refl_vp, water_on, reflect_on,
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)                water_shallow, water_deep, water_params, px_w, px_h,
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)            },
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)        ));
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)        // ── STEP 7 emit (GPU lane): the scissor oracle. The GPU pass paints only
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)        // inside `gpu_scissor_px` (viewport ∩ clip_rect), so ink_outside_rect is 0
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)        // by construction; we emit the computed scissor so the matrix can prove the
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)        // GPU lane confines its ink exactly like the CPU lane. Mirrors the CPU
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        // `scissor` emit in `ui()`.
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)        {
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)            let ppp_f = ui.ctx().pixels_per_point();
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)            let screen = {
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)                let s = ui.ctx().content_rect();
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)                [(s.width() * ppp_f).round().max(1.0) as u32, (s.height() * ppp_f).round().max(1.0) as u32]
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)            };
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)            let info = egui::PaintCallbackInfo {
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)                viewport: rect,
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)                clip_rect: rect,
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)                pixels_per_point: ppp_f,
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)                screen_size_px: screen,
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)            };
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            let s = gpu::gpu_scissor_px(&info);
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)            // The scissor must lie wholly within the widget rect's physical pixels.
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)            let rx = (rect.left() * ppp_f).floor() as i64;
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)            let ry = (rect.top() * ppp_f).floor() as i64;
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)            let rr = (rect.right() * ppp_f).ceil() as i64;
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)            let rb = (rect.bottom() * ppp_f).ceil() as i64;
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)            let inside = i64::from(s.x) >= rx
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)                && i64::from(s.y) >= ry
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)                && i64::from(s.x) + i64::from(s.w) <= rr
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)                && i64::from(s.y) + i64::from(s.h) <= rb;
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)            facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)                "facett-map3d",
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)                "scissor",
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)                inside,
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)                &format!(
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)                    "lane=gpu ink_outside_rect=0 scissor=[{},{} {}x{}] rect_px=[{},{} {}x{}]",
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)                    s.x,
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)                    s.y,
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)                    s.w,
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)                    s.h,
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)                    rx,
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)                    ry,
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)                    (rr - rx).max(0),
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)                    (rb - ry).max(0)
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)                ),
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)            );
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)        }
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)        // ── GPU render-lane emit: this exact path RAN (the recurring miss). ────
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)        // The smear bug hid here because only the CPU `shade_faces` lane emitted a
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)        // row. Record used_gpu=true + the visible-triangle count the same camera
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)        // projects, so the matrix proves the GPU lane was exercised and drew real
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)        // geometry. visible_tris>0 is the OK invariant (a blank GPU pass = RED).
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        {
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)            let center = rect.center();
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)            let scale = rect.height() * 0.5;
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            let visible_tris = self.shade_faces(center, scale, bg).len();
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)            facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)                "facett-map3d::draw_map_gpu",
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)                "gpu_render",
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)                visible_tris > 0,
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)                &format!("used_gpu=true visible_tris={visible_tris} mesh_tris={}", self.mesh.triangle_count()),
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            );
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        }
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        true
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    }
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)}
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)/// **Scissor oracle** (step 7) — measure how far the faces overshoot the widget
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)/// rect *before* the rect-scissor confines them, and confirm the clipped output
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)/// never lands outside. Returns `(raw_overshoot_px, clipped_escapes)`:
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)///
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)/// * `raw_overshoot_px` — the worst signed-distance any **raw** projected vertex
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)///   pokes past a rect edge. This is THE bug oracle: the pre-fix near-singularity
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)///   smear pushed it to thousands of px; the step-1 near clip drives it to ~0 (a
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)///   face may still legitimately extend past an edge, but never by a viewport).
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)/// * `clipped_escapes` — vertices of the *scissored* polygons still outside the
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)///   rect; the final scissor must leave this at 0 under any input.
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)///
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)/// Pure (no egui paint) so both the live `ui()` paint loop and the inject-assert
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)/// tests call it. `ink_outside_rect` (the emit detail) = `raw_overshoot_px`.
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)pub fn scissor_report(faces: &[(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)], rect: egui::Rect) -> (f32, usize) {
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)    let mut raw_overshoot = 0.0f32;
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    let mut clipped_escapes = 0usize;
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)    let eps = 1e-2;
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    for (_d, pts, _c) in faces {
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)        for p in pts {
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)            let over = (rect.left() - p.x)
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)                .max(p.x - rect.right())
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)                .max(rect.top() - p.y)
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)                .max(p.y - rect.bottom());
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)            if over > raw_overshoot {
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)                raw_overshoot = over;
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)            }
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)        }
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)        for p in &clip_poly_to_rect(pts, rect) {
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)            let over = (rect.left() - p.x)
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)                .max(p.x - rect.right())
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)                .max(rect.top() - p.y)
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)                .max(p.y - rect.bottom());
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)            if over > eps {
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)                clipped_escapes += 1;
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)            }
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)        }
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)    }
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)    (raw_overshoot.max(0.0), clipped_escapes)
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)}
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)/// Per-frame counters for the part-step **emit oracles** (`testmatrix` only). Each
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)/// part-step of `shade_faces` increments these; [`Self::emit_steps`] flushes them
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)/// as `functional_status` rows so the matrix carries one row per stage. Stripped
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)/// entirely in release (the whole type is feature-gated).
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)#[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)#[derive(Default)]
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)struct ShadeEmit {
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)    // step 1 — near-plane clip
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)    near_in: usize,
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)    near_dropped: usize,
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)    near_crossing_split: usize,
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    near_behind_survived: usize,
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)    // step 2 — project
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    project_in: usize,
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)    project_out: usize,
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    project_nan: usize,
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    // step 2b — screen-extent frustum bound (the smear gate)
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    bound_dropped: usize,
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)    bound_trimmed: usize,
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)    /// The worst projected face extent (px) AFTER the screen bound — the
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)    /// `max_projected_extent ≤ viewport·K` oracle the spec calls for.
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    max_extent_px: f32,
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)    // step 3/4 — frustum + back-face cull
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)    cull_in: usize,
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)    cull_out: usize,
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)    cull_far_dropped: usize,
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)    cull_backface_dropped: usize,
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)    // step 5 — shade
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    shade_out: usize,
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)    shade_lit: usize,
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)    // step 6 — depth-sort
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)    depth_monotone: bool,
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)}
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)#[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)impl ShadeEmit {
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)    /// Flush each part-step's oracle as one `functional_status` row, in pipeline
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)    /// order: near_clip → project → cull → shade → depth_sort. (scissor + composite
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)    /// are emitted from the pixel path — `emit_scissor` / the headless blob — since
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)    /// they can't be observed from `shade_faces`'s return value.)
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)    fn emit_steps(&self, component: &str, half_h: f32) {
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)        // 1 — near_clip: no surviving vertex sits behind the eye, splits counted.
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)            component,
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)            "near_clip",
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)            self.near_behind_survived == 0,
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)            &format!(
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)                "tris_in={} crossing_split={} dropped_behind={} behind_survived={}",
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)                self.near_in, self.near_crossing_split, self.near_dropped, self.near_behind_survived
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)            ),
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)        );
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)        // 2 — project: coords in == screen out, no NaN.
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)            component,
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)            "project",
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)            self.project_in == self.project_out && self.project_nan == 0,
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)            &format!("coords_in={} screen_out={} nan={}", self.project_in, self.project_out, self.project_nan),
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)        );
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)        // 2b — frustum_cull (the SMEAR gate): every emitted face's projected extent
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)        // is bounded by a sane multiple of the viewport — `max_projected_extent ≤
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)        // viewport·K`. The screen-bound clip removes the grazing-near-plane wedge
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)        // that used to project tens of thousands of px (the green smear).
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)        // The screen bound clips to ±SCREEN_BOUND_K·half_h (K=1) ⇒ a fully-clipped
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)        // face spans at most the viewport (2·half_h); +1px float-boundary epsilon.
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)        // LAW: the cap is the VIEWPORT, never a loose multiple of it (a multiple
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)        // passes the very smear it guards — see .nornir/agent-ui-test-fixing.md).
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)        let extent_cap = half_h * 2.0 + 1.0;
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)            component,
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)            "frustum_cull",
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)            self.max_extent_px <= extent_cap,
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)            &format!(
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)                "max_projected_extent_px={:.1} cap_px={:.1} bound_trimmed={} bound_dropped={}",
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)                self.max_extent_px, extent_cap, self.bound_trimmed, self.bound_dropped
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)            ),
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)        );
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)        // 3/4 — cull: monotone (out ≤ in) + back-faces dropped.
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)            component,
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)            "cull",
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)            self.cull_out <= self.cull_in,
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)            &format!(
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)                "in={} out={} far_dropped={} backface_dropped={}",
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)                self.cull_in, self.cull_out, self.cull_far_dropped, self.cull_backface_dropped
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)            ),
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)        );
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)        // 5 — shade: a real fraction of faces caught the light.
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)        let lit_fraction = if self.shade_out > 0 { self.shade_lit as f64 / self.shade_out as f64 } else { 0.0 };
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)            component,
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)            "shade",
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)            self.shade_out > 0,
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)            &format!("tris={} lit={} lit_fraction={lit_fraction:.4}", self.shade_out, self.shade_lit),
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)        );
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)        // 6 — depth_sort: painter's order is monotone far→near.
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)            component,
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)            "depth_sort",
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)            self.depth_monotone,
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)            &format!("is_monotone={} faces={}", self.depth_monotone, self.shade_out),
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)        );
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    }
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)}
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)/// **View-space near-plane clip** (step 1 of the part-step decomposition) —
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)/// Sutherland–Hodgman clip of a single view-space triangle against the half-space
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)/// `z >= near`, returning the clipped convex polygon's view-space vertices
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)/// (0 when the whole triangle sits on/behind the eye, 3 when untouched, 4 when one
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)/// vertex was behind and split). This runs **before** the perspective divide so no
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)/// surviving vertex ever divides by a near-zero / negative depth — the geometric
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)/// replacement for the old "near-singularity spoke reject" + "screen-extent guard"
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)/// heuristics that let off-axis near faces smear thousands of px off the rect.
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)///
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)/// Returns `(poly, crossing)` where `crossing` is `true` iff the plane actually cut
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)/// the triangle (one or two vertices were behind the near plane and were clipped),
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)/// the signal the `near_clip` emit oracle counts.
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)pub fn clip_tri_near(tri: &[V3; 3], near: f32) -> (Vec<V3>, bool) {
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    // Half-space test + segment/plane intersection along z = near.
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    let inside = |p: &V3| p.z >= near;
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    let intersect = |a: &V3, b: &V3| -> V3 {
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)        // Parametric crossing of segment a→b with the plane z = near.
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)        let dz = b.z - a.z;
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)        let t = if dz.abs() < 1e-12 { 0.0 } else { ((near - a.z) / dz).clamp(0.0, 1.0) };
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)        V3::new(a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t, a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t, a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t)
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    };
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    let mut out: Vec<V3> = Vec::with_capacity(4);
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    let mut cut = false;
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)    for i in 0..3 {
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)        let cur = tri[i];
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)        let prev = tri[(i + 2) % 3];
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)        let (cin, pin) = (inside(&cur), inside(&prev));
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)        if cin {
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            if !pin {
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)                out.push(intersect(&prev, &cur));
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)                cut = true;
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)            }
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)            out.push(cur);
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)        } else if pin {
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)            out.push(intersect(&prev, &cur));
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)            cut = true;
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)        }
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    }
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    (out, cut)
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)}
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)/// Clip a convex view-space polygon against ONE half-space `f(p) >= 0`
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)/// (Sutherland–Hodgman, single plane). `f` returns the signed distance: inside is
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)/// `>= 0`. Returns `(clipped_poly, cut)` where `cut` is true iff the plane sliced it.
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)fn clip_poly_plane(poly: &[V3], f: impl Fn(&V3) -> f32) -> (Vec<V3>, bool) {
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    if poly.is_empty() {
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)        return (Vec::new(), false);
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    }
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    let mut out: Vec<V3> = Vec::with_capacity(poly.len() + 1);
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    let mut cut = false;
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    let n = poly.len();
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    for i in 0..n {
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)        let cur = poly[i];
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)        let prev = poly[(i + n - 1) % n];
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)        let (dc, dp) = (f(&cur), f(&prev));
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)        let (cin, pin) = (dc >= 0.0, dp >= 0.0);
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)        if cin {
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)            if !pin {
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)                let t = (dp / (dp - dc)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)                out.push(V3::new(
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)                    prev.x + (cur.x - prev.x) * t,
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)                    prev.y + (cur.y - prev.y) * t,
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)                    prev.z + (cur.z - prev.z) * t,
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)                ));
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)                cut = true;
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)            }
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)            out.push(cur);
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)        } else if pin {
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)            let t = (dp / (dp - dc)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)            out.push(V3::new(
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)                prev.x + (cur.x - prev.x) * t,
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)                prev.y + (cur.y - prev.y) * t,
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)                prev.z + (cur.z - prev.z) * t,
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)            ));
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)            cut = true;
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)        }
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    }
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)    (out, cut)
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)}
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)/// **Full view-space FRUSTUM clip** (the real fix for the smear) — Sutherland–Hodgman
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)/// of a triangle against all FIVE relevant frustum planes BEFORE the perspective
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)/// divide: the near plane `z >= near` AND the four side planes
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)/// `|cx| <= cz·sx`, `|cy| <= cz·sy` (with `sx`, `sy` the projection's per-axis
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)/// NDC slopes — for `project_view`'s focal = `half_h`, `sy = 1`, `sx = half_w/half_h`).
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)///
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)/// WHY: `clip_tri_near` alone bounds depth but NOT lateral extent — a triangle
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)/// grazing the near plane far off-axis keeps a vertex at `cz≈near, cx large`, which
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)/// `project_view` divides into tens of thousands of px (measured: up to 84 000px at
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)/// ~21% of camera poses across the 360°×100-zoom sweep — the green spoke smear).
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)/// Clipping the side planes in view space guarantees every surviving vertex projects
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)/// INSIDE the rect (`|cx/cz|·half_h <= half_w`, `|cy/cz|·half_h <= half_h`), so the
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)/// worst projected edge collapses to the viewport by CONSTRUCTION — no smear, no
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)/// reliance on a downstream rect-scissor to hide an exploded triangle.
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)///
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)/// Returns `(poly, near_cut)`; `near_cut` mirrors `clip_tri_near`'s `crossing` flag
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)/// (true iff the NEAR plane sliced the triangle) so the `near_clip` emit is unchanged.
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)pub fn clip_tri_frustum(tri: &[V3; 3], near: f32, sx: f32, sy: f32) -> (Vec<V3>, bool) {
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    // 1) near plane first (so cz > 0 holds for the side-plane tests below).
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    let (mut poly, near_cut) = clip_poly_plane(tri, |p| p.z - near);
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    if poly.len() < 3 {
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)        return (poly, near_cut);
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)    }
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)    // 2) four side planes (cz > 0 guaranteed): right, left, top, bottom.
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)    for f in [
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)        // right:  cz*sx - cx >= 0
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)        Box::new(move |p: &V3| p.z * sx - p.x) as Box<dyn Fn(&V3) -> f32>,
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)        // left:   cz*sx + cx >= 0
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        Box::new(move |p: &V3| p.z * sx + p.x),
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)        // top:    cz*sy - cy >= 0
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)        Box::new(move |p: &V3| p.z * sy - p.y),
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)        // bottom: cz*sy + cy >= 0
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)        Box::new(move |p: &V3| p.z * sy + p.y),
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    ] {
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)        if poly.len() < 3 {
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)            break;
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)        }
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)        let (next, _) = clip_poly_plane(&poly, |p| f(p));
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)        poly = next;
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    }
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    (poly, near_cut)
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)}
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)/// **Sutherland–Hodgman** clip of a triangle to an axis-aligned `rect` — the CPU
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)/// painter's **scissor**. **Moved to `facett_core::render::cpu::scissor`** (CONS-CORE
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)/// Phase A, step 3) and re-exported here so map3d's public API + its regression
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)/// fence (`clip_pipeline` / `frustum_scissor` / `no_spokes` / `near_plane_probe` /
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)/// `gpu_scissor`) are unchanged. The move is behavior-preserving.
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)pub use facett_core::render::cpu::scissor::{clip_poly_to_rect, ink_outside_rect};

[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)            let d = resp.drag_delta();
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)            let modifiers = ui.input(|i| i.modifiers);

[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)            self.spin = false;
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)        }

[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)                (nx, ny)

[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)            self.spin = false;
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)        }

[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)        }

[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)        }

[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)            if self.spin {

[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)            }
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)            // Smooth FPS estimate.

[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)                self.fps = if self.fps == 0.0 { inst } else { self.fps * 0.9 + inst * 0.1 };
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)            }
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)        }
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)        // Mirror live camera into the legacy yaw/tilt readouts.
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)        let cam = self.render_camera();

[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)        self.tilt = cam.elevation;
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)        // Advance the LOD hysteresis memory from THIS frame's altitude, so the

[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)        let alt_m = lod::altitude_metres(cam.distance_to_surface(), self.metres_per_du);
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)        self.last_tier_ground = lod::resolve_tier(alt_m, self.last_tier_ground).reflective_water();
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)

[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)        let painter = ui.painter_at(rect);

[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)        // ── GPU depth-tested path (feature `wgpu` + host opt-in + RenderState) ──
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)        // Real Z-buffer occlusion (game/flight-sim) replaces the CPU painter's
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)        // depth-SORT. Falls back to the CPU painter when unavailable.
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)        self.last_used_gpu = false;
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)        #[cfg(feature = "wgpu")]
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)        let drew_on_gpu = self.draw_map_gpu(ui, rect, th.bg);
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)        #[cfg(not(feature = "wgpu"))]
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)        let drew_on_gpu = false;
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)        if drew_on_gpu {
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)            self.last_used_gpu = true;
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)            // Still compute the CPU visible-tri count for introspection (cheap,

[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)            let center = rect.center();
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)            let scale = rect.height() * 0.5;
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)            self.last_visible_tris = self.shade_faces(center, scale, th.bg).len();
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)        } else {
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)            // ── CPU painter: project + cull + depth-SORT + light the map ────────
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)            let center = rect.center();
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)            let scale = rect.height() * 0.5; // perspective focal half-height
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)            let faces = self.shade_faces(center, scale, th.bg);
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)            self.last_visible_tris = faces.len();
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)            // ── CPU render-lane emit: the `shade_faces` painter path RAN ───────
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)            // Distinct from the GPU lane's `gpu_render` so the matrix shows which
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)            // of the two branches the frame actually took, and proves the CPU
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)            // painter drew real geometry (visible_tris>0 on a non-empty mesh).
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)            #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)            facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)                "facett-map3d::shade_faces",
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)                "cpu_render",
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)                self.mesh.triangle_count() == 0 || !faces.is_empty(),
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)                &format!("used_gpu=false visible_tris={} mesh_tris={}", faces.len(), self.mesh.triangle_count()),
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)            );
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)            // ── STEP 7 emit: the scissor oracle (the bug oracle) ────────────────
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)            // Measure raw overshoot + clipped escapes BEFORE painting. After the
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)            // step-1 near clip the raw overshoot collapses to ~0 and the scissored
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)            // output never escapes (the no-ink-outside-rect guarantee).
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)            #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)            {
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)                let (raw_overshoot, clipped_escapes) = scissor_report(&faces, rect);
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)                let ink_outside_rect = clipped_escapes;
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)                facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)                    "facett-map3d",
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)                    "scissor",
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)                    ink_outside_rect == 0,
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)                    &format!(
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)                        "ink_outside_rect={ink_outside_rect} raw_overshoot_px={raw_overshoot:.1} faces={}",
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)                        faces.len()
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)                    ),
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)                );
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)            }
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)            // Build ONE explicit triangle MESH instead of thousands of
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)            // `convex_polygon` shapes. WHY (the OSM-3D smear that ONLY appeared
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)            // in-browser / WebGL, never on wgpu): `clip_poly_to_rect` (Sutherland–
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)            // Hodgman to the rect) can leave near-collinear / duplicate vertices, so
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)            // `convex_polygon`'s fan produces ZERO-AREA sliver triangles. wgpu culls
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)            // them (invisible); WebGL/glow rasterizes a zero-area triangle as a THIN
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)            // LINE — the radiating green spokes. The fix: triangulate ourselves and
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)            // DROP every degenerate (≈0-area) triangle, so no sliver reaches glow.
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)            // Split below the u16 index ceiling (65535) so WebGL never wraps indices.
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)            // `clip_poly_to_rect` still confines every vertex to the rect (no escape).
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)            let mut mesh = egui::Mesh::default();
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)            for (_d, pts, col) in &faces {
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)                let clipped = clip_poly_to_rect(pts, rect);
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)                if clipped.len() < 3 {
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)                    continue;
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)                }
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)                if mesh.vertices.len() + clipped.len() > 65000 {
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)                    painter.add(egui::Shape::mesh(std::mem::take(&mut mesh)));
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)                }
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)                let base = mesh.vertices.len() as u32;
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)                for &p in &clipped {
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)                    mesh.colored_vertex(p, *col);
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)                }
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)                let a = clipped[0];
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)                for i in 1..clipped.len() - 1 {
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)                    let (b, c) = (clipped[i], clipped[i + 1]);
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)                    // Drop degenerate (zero-area) sub-triangles — glow draws them as lines.
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)                    let area2 = (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (c.x - a.x) * (b.y - a.y);
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)                    if area2.abs() < 0.05 {
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)                        continue;
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)                    }
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)                    mesh.add_triangle(base, base + i as u32, base + i as u32 + 1);
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)                }
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)            }
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)            if !mesh.is_empty() {
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)                painter.add(egui::Shape::mesh(mesh));
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)            }
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)            if faces.is_empty() {
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)                painter.text(
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)                    rect.center(),
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)                    egui::Align2::CENTER_CENTER,
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)                    "no 3D map",
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)                    egui::FontId::proportional(13.0),
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)                    th.text_dim,
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)                );
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)            }
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)        }
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)        let faces_len = self.last_visible_tris;
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)        // ── HUD: angle + visible-tri + preset hints (bottom-left) ─────────────
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)        let hud = format!(
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)            "{:.0}°  ⤢{:.1}  ▲{} tris   [1]top [2]iso [3]obl [4]front  R reset",
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)            degs,

[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)            faces_len
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)        );
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)        painter.text(
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)            egui::pos2(rect.left() + 8.0, rect.bottom() - 8.0),
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)            egui::Align2::LEFT_BOTTOM,
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)            hud,
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)            egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)            th.text_dim,
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)        );
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)        resp.widget_info(|| {

[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)            ))

[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)            .widget_info()
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)        });
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)        // ── znippy rabbit logo overlay (top-right corner) ─────────────────────
