[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)    fn caps(&self) -> FacetCaps {
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)        // Navigable: the orbit camera does dolly (zoom-to-cursor), orbit, pan,
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)        // view presets + reset — the shared pan/zoom/fit model, in 3D.
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)        FacetCaps::NONE.themeable().resizable().navigable()
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)    }
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)    // ── cross-instance clone (copy/paste BETWEEN two Map3D views) ─────────────
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)    fn kind(&self) -> &'static str {
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)        "map3d"
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)    }
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)    /// The portable **camera pose**: orbit target, azimuth, elevation, dolly
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)    /// distance, and field of view — the 3/4-view a sibling `map3d` can adopt to
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)    /// frame its own city from the same angle. (The basemap mesh is each view's
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)    /// own; this clones where the camera SITS.)
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    fn portable_state(&self) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)        let c = &self.cam;
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)        Some(serde_json::json!({
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)            "target": [c.target.x, c.target.y, c.target.z],
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)            "azimuth": c.azimuth,
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)            "elevation": c.elevation,
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)            "distance": c.distance,
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)            "fov_y": c.fov_y,
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)        }))
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    }
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)    fn load_state(&mut self, state: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)        let obj = match state.as_object() {
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)            Some(o) => o,
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)            None => return false,
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)        };
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)        let f = |k: &str| obj.get(k).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()).map(|v| v as f32);
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        if let Some(t) = obj.get("target").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)            if let (Some(x), Some(y), Some(z)) = (
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)                t.first().and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)                t.get(1).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)                t.get(2).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)            ) {
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)                let v = V3::new(x as f32, y as f32, z as f32);
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)                self.cam.target = v;
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)                self.cam.goal_target = v;
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)            }
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)        }
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)        if let Some(a) = f("azimuth") {
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)            self.cam.azimuth = a;
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)            self.cam.goal_azimuth = a;
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)            self.yaw = a; // keep the legacy snapshot angle in sync
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)        }
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)        if let Some(e) = f("elevation") {
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)            self.cam.elevation = e;
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)            self.cam.goal_elevation = e;
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)            self.tilt = e;
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)        }
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)        if let Some(d) = f("distance") {
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)            self.cam.distance = d;
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)            self.cam.goal_distance = d;
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)        }
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)        if let Some(fov) = f("fov_y") {
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)            self.cam.fov_y = fov;
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)        }
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)        true
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    }
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)}
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)

[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)    #[test]
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)    fn portable_state_round_trips_camera_pose_between_instances() {
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)        use facett_core::clipboard;
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)        // A: a synthetic map framed at a specific pose.
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        let mut a = Map3D::synthetic("A");
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        a.cam.target = V3::new(1.0, 0.2, -3.0);
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)        a.cam.azimuth = 0.9;
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)        a.cam.elevation = 0.6;
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)        a.cam.distance = 5.5;
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)        a.cam.fov_y = 42f32.to_radians();
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)        let env = clipboard::encode_component(a.kind(), &a.portable_state().unwrap());
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)        let (kind, state) = clipboard::decode_component(&env).unwrap();
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)        assert_eq!(kind, "map3d");
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)        // B is a different synthetic map at the default pose.
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)        let mut b = Map3D::synthetic("B");
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)        assert_ne!(b.portable_state(), a.portable_state(), "differ before paste");
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)        assert!(b.load_state(&state));
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)        assert_eq!(b.portable_state(), a.portable_state(), "B mirrors A's camera pose");
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)        // The damping goals were set too, so the live camera settles at the pose.
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)        assert_eq!(b.cam.goal_distance, 5.5);
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)        assert_eq!(b.cam.goal_azimuth, 0.9);
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)    }

[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)    fn building(ring: &[(f64, f64)]) -> Way {
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)        let tags: Vec<(String, String)> =
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)            vec![("building".to_string(), "yes".to_string())];
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)        Way::from_lonlat(1, ring, &tags, &Theme::default()).expect("a building way")
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)    }
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)    /// A grid of `n×n` small building footprints over a ~1.5 km town (the real
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)    /// city the demo extrudes), each a closed `building=yes` ring with a unique id.
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)    fn town_grid(n: usize) -> Vec<Way> {
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)        let mut ways = Vec::with_capacity(n * n);
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)        let (lon0, lat0) = (17.70_f64, 59.61_f64); // inside the Sigtuna bbox
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)        let step = 0.003;
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)        let bsz = 0.0008;
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)        let mut id = 1i64;
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)        for r in 0..n {
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)            for c in 0..n {
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)                let bx = lon0 + c as f64 * step;
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)                let by = lat0 + r as f64 * step;
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)                let ring = [(bx, by), (bx + bsz, by), (bx + bsz, by + bsz), (bx, by + bsz), (bx, by)];
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)                let tags = vec![("building".to_string(), "yes".to_string())];
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)                ways.push(Way::from_lonlat(id, &ring, &tags, &Theme::default()).unwrap());
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)                id += 1;
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)            }
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)        }
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)        ways
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)    }
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)    /// **PART-B test 1 — N building ways → N extruded prisms, every face inside the
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    /// widget rect.** Inject a 5×5 town (25 buildings) → assert `tile_count` = 25
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)    /// prisms + 1 terrain, and that at the framed default camera every shaded face
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)    /// the painter would draw clips to a polygon entirely inside the rect (the
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)    /// no-ink-outside-rect guarantee holds for the real city path, not just a fixture).
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)    #[test]
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)    fn n_building_ways_extrude_to_n_prisms_inside_rect() {
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)        let ways = town_grid(5);
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)        assert_eq!(ways.len(), 25);
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)        let mut m = Map3D::from_geometry("city", &ways);
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)        m.spin = false;
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)        m.cam.settle();
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)        // 25 building prisms + the terrain plane.
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)        assert_eq!(m.tile_count(), 26, "25 prisms + 1 terrain plane");
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)        // Render the faces and clip each to the rect — none may escape it.
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)        let rect = egui::Rect::from_min_max(Pos2::new(100.0, 80.0), Pos2::new(820.0, 700.0));
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)        let center = rect.center();
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)        let scale = rect.height() * 0.5;
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)        let faces = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::from_rgb(20, 24, 40));
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)        assert!(!faces.is_empty(), "the framed city projects visible faces");
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)        let eps = 1e-2;
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        for (_d, pts, _c) in &faces {
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)            let clipped = clip_poly_to_rect(pts, rect);
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)            for p in &clipped {
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)                assert!(
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)                    p.x >= rect.left() - eps && p.x <= rect.right() + eps
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)                        && p.y >= rect.top() - eps && p.y <= rect.bottom() + eps,
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)                    "a clipped face vertex {p:?} escaped the widget rect"
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)                );
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)            }
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)        }
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    }
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)    /// **PART-B test 2 — buildings are VISIBLE at the default camera (non-trivial
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)    /// vertical extent).** The whole point: on open, the city must read as risen
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    /// 3D, not a flat field. Build the real-data path (`from_geometry`, which frames
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    /// the densest cluster + dollies in) and assert the projected faces span a real
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)    /// vertical pixel range AND the mesh actually rose off the ground.
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    #[test]
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)    fn buildings_are_visible_at_default_camera() {
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)        let ways = town_grid(6); // 36 buildings → a dense enough town
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)        let mut m = Map3D::from_geometry("city", &ways);
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)        m.spin = false;
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)        m.cam.settle();
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)        // The mesh rose off the ground (real prisms, not flat cover).
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)        let ymax = m.mesh().positions.iter().map(|p| p[1]).fold(f32::MIN, f32::max);
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)        assert!(ymax > 1e-3, "buildings extruded upward (ymax={ymax})");
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)        // At the DEFAULT framed camera the projected city occupies a real vertical
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)        // band of the viewport — not a sub-pixel ridge.
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)        let center = Pos2::new(450.0, 450.0);
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)        let scale = 450.0;
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)        let faces = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::from_rgb(20, 24, 40));
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)        assert!(!faces.is_empty(), "the framed city is visible on open");
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)        let (mut ytop, mut ybot) = (f32::MAX, f32::MIN);
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)        for (_d, pts, _c) in &faces {
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)            for p in pts {
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)                ytop = ytop.min(p.y);
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)                ybot = ybot.max(p.y);
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)            }
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)        }
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)        let vspan = ybot - ytop;
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)        // A flat field would project to a near-zero vertical band; a risen city
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)        // fills a substantial fraction of the 900 px viewport.
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)        assert!(vspan > 40.0, "the city has a real vertical extent on open (vspan={vspan:.1}px)");
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    }

[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)    /// INJECT-ASSERT: feed two real closed building rings → assert the extruded
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)    /// mesh has real geometry (verts/tris > 0), one prism per ring + the terrain
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)    /// = 3 footprints, and z spans a real height (it was actually lifted).

[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    }

[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)    /// INJECT-ASSERT: with a fixed clock, shading produces real lit faces (a
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)    /// non-empty, depth-sorted face list) — the CPU path actually drew the model.
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)    #[test]
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)    fn shading_produces_lit_depth_sorted_faces() {
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)        let m = Map3D::synthetic("r").with_clock(1.0);
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)        let faces = m.shade_faces(Pos2::new(400.0, 300.0), 200.0, Color32::WHITE);
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)        assert!(!faces.is_empty(), "the orbited, lit, culled model produced visible faces");
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)        // Painter's algorithm: far (large camera depth) first → near last, so the
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)        // emitted depths are NON-INCREASING.
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)        for w in faces.windows(2) {
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)            assert!(w[0].0 >= w[1].0 - 1e-3, "faces are depth-sorted far→near");
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)        }
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)        // The faces carry distinct shades (lighting actually varied them).
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)        let mut shades = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)        for (_d, _p, c) in &faces {
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)            shades.insert((c.r(), c.g(), c.b()));
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)        }
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)        assert!(shades.len() >= 3, "lighting yields multiple shades, got {}", shades.len());
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)    }

[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)    /// Discovery-contract: local()/remote() build a renderable 3D-map facet whose
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)    /// state_json reports the camera pose + footprint/triangle counts. The test
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)    /// matrix enumerates a facet by these ctors (mirrors OsmView::local/remote).
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)    #[test]
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    fn local_and_remote_ctors_build_a_drawable_3d_facet() {
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)        use facett_core::harness;
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)        for (mut m, want_title) in [(Map3D::local(), "OSM 3D"), (Map3D::remote(), "OSM 3D (remote)")] {
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)            m.set_clock(1.0); // a fixed clock so the orbit is a pure function
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)            let r = harness::headless_render(&mut m);
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)            assert_eq!(r.title, want_title);
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)            assert!(r.drew(), "the lit extruded skyline tessellates to vertices");
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)            assert!(r.state["triangles"].as_u64().unwrap() > 50, "real mesh");
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)            assert!(r.state["tiles"].as_u64().unwrap() >= 5, "rabbit loops + terrain");
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)            assert!(r.state["visible_triangles"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0, "the camera projected visible tris");

[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    /// INJECT-ASSERT (navigation): feed the real extruded skyline, then **orbit
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)    /// the camera** and confirm the model stays visible AND the projected pixels
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)    /// actually moved — i.e. we are "viewing from a different angle", not the same
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)    /// frame. This proves the camera drives the render, not a fixed transform.
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    #[test]
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)    fn orbiting_the_camera_changes_the_view_but_keeps_it_visible() {
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)        let mut m = Map3D::synthetic("nav");
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)        m.spin = false; // hold the angle so the orbit delta is the only change
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)        let center = Pos2::new(400.0, 300.0);
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)        let scale = 300.0;
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)        let before = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::WHITE);
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)        assert!(!before.is_empty(), "the model is visible before orbiting");
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)        let centroid = |fs: &[(f32, [Pos2; 3], Color32)]| {
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)            let (mut sx, mut sy) = (0.0f32, 0.0f32);
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)            let mut n = 0.0f32;
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)            for (_d, p, _c) in fs {
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)                for v in p {
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)                    sx += v.x;
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)                    sy += v.y;
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)                    n += 1.0;
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)                }
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)            }
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)            (sx / n, sy / n)
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)        };
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)        let c0 = centroid(&before);
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)        // Orbit ~30° around and settle the damping so the new angle is exact.
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)        m.cam.orbit(400.0, 60.0);
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)        m.cam.settle();
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)        let after = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::WHITE);
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)        assert!(!after.is_empty(), "the model is STILL visible after orbiting");
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)        let c1 = centroid(&after);
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)        let moved = ((c1.0 - c0.0).powi(2) + (c1.1 - c0.1).powi(2)).sqrt();
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        assert!(moved > 1.0, "orbiting actually re-projected the model (moved {moved:.2}px)");
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)    }
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)    /// INJECT-ASSERT (presets): each view preset puts the camera at the
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)    /// documented angle, and the resulting projection differs from the others —
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)    /// proving "view from different angles" presets are wired to the math.
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)    #[test]
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)    fn view_presets_are_distinct_camera_angles() {
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)        let mut m = Map3D::synthetic("presets");
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)        m.spin = false;
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)        let center = Pos2::new(400.0, 300.0);
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)        let scale = 300.0;
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)        // Top-down: elevation ≈ +90°, so the eye is almost straight above target.
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)        m.view_preset(ViewPreset::Top);
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)        m.cam.settle();
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)        let top_el = m.cam.elevation;
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)        assert!(top_el > 1.5, "top preset looks down (elevation {top_el:.3} rad)");
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)        let top_eye = m.cam.eye();
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)        assert!(top_eye.y > m.cam.target.y + m.cam.distance * 0.9, "top eye is high above target");
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)        // Front: nearly level.
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)        m.view_preset(ViewPreset::Front);
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)        m.cam.settle();
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)        assert!(m.cam.elevation < 0.2, "front preset is ~level, got {}", m.cam.elevation);
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)        // The two presets render visibly different frames.
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)        m.view_preset(ViewPreset::Top);
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)        m.cam.settle();
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)        let top_faces = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::WHITE).len();
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)        m.view_preset(ViewPreset::Oblique);
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)        m.cam.settle();
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)        let obl_faces = m.shade_faces(center, scale, Color32::WHITE).len();
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)        assert!(top_faces > 0 && obl_faces > 0, "both presets draw the model");
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    }

[2039](https://docs.rs#2039)
[2040](https://docs.rs#2040)    /// INJECT-ASSERT (the **scissor**): `clip_poly_to_rect` confines every face to
[2041](https://docs.rs#2041)    /// the widget rect. A triangle whose verts sprawl thousands of px outside the
[2042](https://docs.rs#2042)    /// rect (the off-axis foreground / near-singularity smear) clips to a polygon
[2043](https://docs.rs#2043)    /// **entirely inside** the rect; one wholly outside clips to empty (dropped);
[2044](https://docs.rs#2044)    /// one already inside is unchanged. Proves no CPU-painter ink can escape the rect.
[2045](https://docs.rs#2045)    #[test]
[2046](https://docs.rs#2046)    fn clip_poly_to_rect_confines_every_vertex_to_the_rect() {
[2047](https://docs.rs#2047)        let rect = egui::Rect::from_min_max(Pos2::new(100.0, 100.0), Pos2::new(500.0, 500.0));
[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)        let eps = 1e-3;
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)        let inside = |p: &Pos2| {
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)            p.x >= rect.left() - eps && p.x <= rect.right() + eps && p.y >= rect.top() - eps && p.y <= rect.bottom() + eps
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)        };
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)        // A face sprawling far outside the rect on every side (the smear) → its clip
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)        // is a non-empty polygon whose EVERY vertex sits inside the rect.
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)        let sprawl = [Pos2::new(-4000.0, 300.0), Pos2::new(4000.0, -4000.0), Pos2::new(4000.0, 4000.0)];
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)        let c = clip_poly_to_rect(&sprawl, rect);
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)        assert!(c.len() >= 3, "a face crossing the rect still produces a polygon");
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)        assert!(c.iter().all(inside), "every clipped vertex is inside the rect: {c:?}");
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)        // A face wholly outside the rect clips to empty → nothing drawn.
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)        let outside = [Pos2::new(-100.0, -100.0), Pos2::new(-50.0, -100.0), Pos2::new(-100.0, -50.0)];
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)        assert!(clip_poly_to_rect(&outside, rect).len() < 3, "a fully-outside face is dropped");
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)        // A face already inside is preserved (still inside, real area).
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)        let within = [Pos2::new(200.0, 200.0), Pos2::new(300.0, 200.0), Pos2::new(250.0, 300.0)];
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)        let cw = clip_poly_to_rect(&within, rect);
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)        assert!(cw.len() >= 3 && cw.iter().all(inside), "an inside face is kept inside");
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)    }

Re-export so a host can build the rabbit logo overlay without depending on facett-graph3d directly. The 3D extruded-rabbit logo viewer.

}## Expand description

A 3D map viewer: extruded ways + a terrain plane, orbited by a camera.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.title)

`title: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.yaw)

`yaw: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)Orbit yaw (radians) about Y + a fixed tilt about X for a 3/4 city view.
**Legacy** view angles kept for the snapshot/example paths; the live
navigation now flows through [ Self::cam](https://docs.rs/struct.Map3D.html#structfield.cam).

`yaw` mirrors the camera
azimuth and `tilt` the camera elevation so old callers still read sane
values.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.tilt)

`tilt: `[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.spin)

`cam: `[OrbitCamera](https://docs.rs/camera/struct.OrbitCamera.html)The **navigable orbit camera** — the state-of-the-art view: orbit, dolly
(zoom-to-cursor), pan, presets, damped/inertial. Drives the perspective
projection in [ Self::shade_faces](https://docs.rs/struct.Map3D.html#method.shade_faces).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Build a 3D map from real OSM [ Way](https://docs.rs/facett-map/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_map/struct.Way.html)s + an extrusion height scale. Closed
area/building rings are extruded to prisms; line ways become ground ribbons;
a terrain plane is fitted under the data.

`height` is the design-space lift

`Self::from_ways`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#359-410)#### pub fn [frame_densest_cluster](https://docs.rs#method.frame_densest_cluster)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#359-410)

#### pub fn [frame_densest_cluster](https://docs.rs#method.frame_densest_cluster)(&mut self)

Find the **densest cluster of risen (building) geometry** in the extruded
mesh and point the camera at it, dollied in so the cluster fills the view.
Buildings are the `y > 0` (lifted) vertices; ground cover / terrain lie flat
at `y = 0`. We bin the risen vertices into a coarse grid, pick the heaviest
cell, then set the camera target to that cell’s centroid and the distance to
the cluster’s extent — so a country-scale dataset still shows a real town.

The camera actually projected this frame: the live [ Self::cam](https://docs.rs/struct.Map3D.html#structfield.cam), but with
the auto-spin (and any injected clock) folded into its azimuth so a fixed
clock yields a pure, reproducible orbit. Pan/zoom/preset state is preserved.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#593-595)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#593-595)

Project + frustum/back-face cull + depth-sort + light the extruded mesh
into screen-space shaded faces via the **perspective orbit camera**. Pure
(no egui) so the self-test can count *visible lit triangles* without a UI.
Returns `(camera_depth, [3 px], shaded_color)` per visible tri, far→near.

`center` is the viewport centre in pixels; `scale` is the projection
half-height in pixels (≈ half the viewport height) — the perspective focal
scale. `base` is the **atmospheric fog colour** (the background): distant
faces are blended toward it so the city recedes into haze — the subtle depth
cue that, with the directional light, makes the model read as a 3D city
rather than a flat field of prisms. The per-triangle source colour drives the
lit tint; fog only desaturates it with distance.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#605-850)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_map3d/lib.rs.html#605-850)

**Diagnostic / regression variant** of [ Self::shade_faces](https://docs.rs/struct.Map3D.html#method.shade_faces) with the step-1
view-space near clip togglable.

`near_clip = true` is the production path
(the FIX); `near_clip = false` reproduces the *pre-fix*pipeline — the brittle “drop the whole triangle if any vertex is behind the eye” + “screen-extent guard” heuristics — so a fail-on-bug / pass-on-fix test can inject the same camera pose into both and compare the escaping geometry the rect-scissor is then handed. Not for production callers; the bug oracle test uses it to prove the fix changes the geometry that reaches the rasterizer.

# facett_core::rabbit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/rabbit/index.html

## Expand description

**The znippy rabbit** — facett’s synthetic/test mascot, as reusable
*parametric* geometry. znippy ships no logo asset, so the rabbit is generated
here: a friendly sitting-rabbit silhouette (rounded body + head + two upright
ears + an eye dot), built from deterministic arcs in a normalised `[-1, 1]²`
design box (x right, y **up**). No RNG, no per-frame randomness — two calls
produce byte-identical geometry, so the wgpu/CPU snapshots stay stable.

Two consumers share this one source of truth:

- **2D**—- `rabbit_outline`
- **3D**—- `rabbit_mesh`- *extrudes*the silhouette into a solid logo (front + back faces + side walls, with per-vertex normals), which facett-graph3d’s wgpu engine lights and slowly spins.

Both are pure functions of a [ Rabbit](https://docs.rs/struct.Rabbit.html) parameter set, so the look is tunable
without touching either renderer.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Rabbit](https://docs.rs/struct.Rabbit.html)
- Parametric knobs for the rabbit silhouette. All in the normalised `[-1, 1]`design box (y**up**).`Rabbit::default`
- [Rabbit](https://docs.rs/struct.RabbitMesh.html)- Mesh
- A triangle-soup mesh of the extruded rabbit logo: interleaved positions +
normals, indexed. Coordinates are in the `[-1, 1]`design box (y up) with the extrusion along**z**(`±depth/2`). Pure data — the renderer (wgpu or the CPU fallback) projects + lights it.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [rabbit_](https://docs.rs/fn.rabbit_mesh.html)- mesh
- Extrude the rabbit silhouette into a solid 3D logo: a **front**face at`z = +depth/2`, a**back**face at`z = -depth/2`, and the**side walls**joining their rims. Each silhouette loop becomes its own extruded shell (body, head, two ears) — they read as one fused logo when lit.`depth`is the total thickness in design units (~0.3 looks like a chunky logo).
- [rabbit_](https://docs.rs/fn.rabbit_outline.html)- outline
- Convenience: the default mascot’s outline loops. See `Rabbit::outline`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Loop](https://docs.rs/type.Loop.html)
- One closed loop of `(x, y)`vertices in the`[-1, 1]`design box (y up). The first vertex is**not**repeated at the end; close it yourself if you stroke it as a ring. Loops are returned outer-first.
